correctness.rationale: Draisma et al. Corollary 2.10 gives equality for a general complete intersection and, in projective dimension two, specializes to product(d_i) times 1+T+(T^2+Q)/2. For a balancing move x<y-1 with delta=y-x-1, the pair product rises from B to B+delta while the symmetric factor falls from A to A-delta, so the change has sign delta(A-B-delta). Since B+delta=(x+2)y and A-(x+2)y is at least 1+x^2+x+y^2-y>0, every genuine balancing move strictly increases ED degree. Iteration yields the unique balanced maximum; reversing moves yields the unique one-heavy minimum. An independently written exhaustive replay over 425 multidegrees for 2<=c<=6 and 2c<=S<=4c reproduced both extrema and the examples.
risks: The claim is only for generic projective ED degree of smooth complex surfaces; special coordinates may lower ED degree.

value.rationale: ED degree is the algebraic complexity of generic nearest-point optimization. Fixing c and S fixes the canonical polarization exponent for these surfaces, so the comparison is geometrically natural. The theorem gives both sharp extrema and a strict balancing mechanism over an infinite family, not an arbitrary numerical slice.

final_claim: For general smooth complete-intersection surfaces of fixed codimension c and fixed total defining degree S, generic Euclidean distance degree is uniquely maximized, up to permutation, by the balanced multidegree and uniquely minimized by (2,...,2,S-2c+2).
limitations: General smooth complex complete-intersection surfaces only.
